title: The battle inside
hookLine: the fiercest fight in the Granth is with the five thieves in your own mind

lines: A DAY LOST FROM THE INSIDE.
cards: No army, no siege, no broken oath.
Just an ordinary day that went wrong from the inside: a snapped word at someone loved, an hour scrolled away that wasn't there to spare, a grab for the bigger slice, the last word, the credit.

For a week this path has talked about swords. Open the Guru Granth Sahib looking for battles, though, and the ones it keeps returning to have no armies in them. Its fiercest fight happens somewhere else.

teach.b: The Granth names the enemy many times, and it has five faces: kaam, desire that grabs; krodh, anger; lobh, greed; moh, clinging to what we can't keep; and ahankar, pride. These are the five thieves you met weeks ago.
Today, the line that turns them into a battle. It's in Guru Nanak's Japji, the morning prayer, in the twenty-eighth verse.

teach.h: JAPJI 28: THE YOGI'S GEAR TURNED INWARD.
teach.b: That verse speaks to the yogis of Guru Nanak's day and turns their outward gear inward: make contentment your earrings, meditation the ash on your body, faith your staff.
Then it closes on a short line: man jeetai jag jeet.

teach.h: CONQUER THE MIND, CONQUER THE WORLD.
teach.b: Conquer your own mind, and you've conquered the world. Hold that up against this whole week. The saint-soldier's courage.
The kirpan, mercy first. Every other means first. Fair, even in conflict.
The calm face in gatka. Each one depends on winning an inner fight first: against anger that wants to strike, pride that wants to win, fear that wants to run.
A soldier who hasn't fought the five thieves isn't a saint-soldier, just a soldier.
The Granth's weapons for this fight aren't steel. The Name, remembered. The sangat, the company of good people.
The Guru's word. Honest work and sharing. And humility, the opposite of ahankar.
Sikhs don't speak of winning it once and for all. It's a daily fight, and the wins are often small: one sharp word not said, one craving let pass.
That's the battle the whole week pointed to.

how: Sikhs speak of the five thieves (kaam, krodh, lobh, moh, ahankar) as the real enemies, and fight them through naam simran, the sangat, the Guru's word, honest work and humility.

o: the inner peace that comes from prayer
a long journey on foot to a holy place
pride, one of the five thieves in the mind

games.q: the five thieves — tap the pairs.
p: conquer the mind, conquer the world

s: the Guru Granth Sahib is mostly about battles with armies
its fiercest fight is with the five thieves inside the mind.
the Japji says conquering the mind is conquering the world
man jeetai jag jeet, in the twenty-eighth verse.
Sikhs expect to beat the five thieves once and for all
it's a daily fight, and the wins are often small.

games.q: you're a saint-soldier. what fight comes first?
o: the one against the nearest enemy army.
the one against anger, greed and pride in your own mind.
the one you're most likely to win.
games.why: the Granth's fiercest fight is inside. without it the soldier is only a soldier.

practice: Take an honest look inward: which of the five is loudest in you today, anger, greed, desire, clinging or pride? Don't fight it yet; just name it quietly, the way you'd name a visitor.
Then choose one small win against it: one word you won't say, or one thing you'll let go of.

wordCard.voice: Ahankar. Pride, one of the five thieves that wage the battle inside; conquer your own mind, and you've conquered the world.

orig.note: Gurmukhi, from the Japji, verse 28: conquer the mind, and you conquer the world.

carryVoice: Your line: the real battle. Its weapons aren't steel. That closes sword and saint, on day two hundred eighty-one.

sources.ref: Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 600 (Sorath, Guru Amar Das): five thieves within the body
